policy: memory suffixes binary (bare = MiB); disk suffixes decimal (bare = GB); K rejected for disk
bug_report: Since we migrated configs to the new parser, pods are being OOM-killed right after deploy - containers come up with less memory than their config asks for - and disk quotas also look slightly off on some volumes. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix parse_quantity so provisioned resources match the configs, without breaking existing behaviour.
non_guessable: decision lives in git history (a documented commit), broken by a misleading 'perf' regression commit; git log/blame is the shortcut
decision_subject: fix: parse_quantity unit semantics per the provisioning vendor API
decision_rationale: Migrated configs were misprovisioning because parse_quantity treated every suffix as decimal and bare numbers as raw bytes. Vendor API semantics: memory suffixes are binary (K=1024, M=1024**2, G=1024**3, T=1024**4, case-insensitive) and a bare memory number means MiB; disk suffixes are decimal (G=1000**3) and a bare disk number means GB; 'K' is rejected for disk with a ValueError - the vendor API has no kilobyte disk unit and a silent guess would misprovision the volume.
